finding.found_by: the R114 auditor (F93): the disclosed arrhenius_rate_ratio Ea/R magnitude bug is real — 1000x in the EXPONENT
finding.defect: physics_checks.arrhenius_rate_ratio computed exponent = -float(ea.magnitude / (R_GAS.magnitude * 1000)) * (1/T2 - 1/T1) — but ea.magnitude is ALREADY J/mol (pint converted the kJ/mol input at the top of the function), so dividing by (R * 1000) divides by 1000 TWICE; every computed magnitude was wrong by 1000x in the exponent (e.g. the committed reference scenario Ea=80 kJ/mol, 60->80 degC: quoted 1.0016369748, true 5.1327234711)
finding.introduced: R50, commit ebacc1c3a (the physics_checks engine slice, P0.2+P0.3+P1.1)
finding.why_it_survived: every test on the relation was SIGN-ONLY (test_arrhenius_known_answer_directions asserts >1/<1/==1; the F-V5 saturation pins asserted the clamp path; the on-row binding consumed direction); the one magnitude-carrying pin (test_arrhenius_exponent_saturation_disclosed_in_band's in-range tail) asserted 1.0 < value < 1.01 — pinning the BUGGY magnitude itself. The unit-checked r54 reimplementation existed since R54 but nobody cross-compared ENGINE magnitudes against DRIVER magnitudes for this relation
